2	name: vendored-skill-install
3	description: "Installing a third-party skill so Claude Code, Codex and Cowork can all use it — the canonical store, the two symlinks, the CLI flag trap, and why Cowork is different"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: a6dfb3da-c339-44b1-a836-2a6884e07ea6
8	  modified: 2026-09-04T13:43:21.110Z
9	---
10	
11	Third-party skills live in **`~/.agents/skills/<name>/`** (the real files, ~360 of
12	them) with `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` as the install ledger. Both harness
13	directories are symlinks into it:
14	
15	- `~/.claude/skills/<name>` → `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (relative)
16	- `~/.codex/skills/<name>` → `~/.claude/skills/<name>` (absolute, hopping through
17	  the Claude symlink — verified on disk 2026-09-04. It does **not** point straight
18	  at `~/.agents/skills/`.)
19	
20	Install with the CLI that owns that store when you can:
21	
22	```bash
23	npx -y skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> -g -a claude-code -a codex -s <skill> -y
24	```
25	
26	**Trap: in Claude Code auto mode the CLI itself is blocked.** The permission
27	classifier denies `npx -y skills@latest add …` outright (hit 2026-09-04).
28	Hand-install is then the working route, and it is enough — the files plus the two
29	symlinks are all a harness needs:
30	
31	```bash
32	mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills/NAME
33	cp REPO/CAT/NAME/SKILL.md ~/.agents/skills/NAME/
34	cp -R REPO/CAT/NAME/scripts REPO/CAT/NAME/agents ~/.agents/skills/NAME/   # when present
35	chmod +x ~/.agents/skills/NAME/scripts/*.sh
36	ln -s ../../.agents/skills/NAME ~/.claude/skills/NAME
37	ln -s ~/.claude/skills/NAME ~/.codex/skills/NAME
38	```
39	
40	Copy `agents/openai.yaml` too whenever the skill ships one — it is the
41	Codex-facing manifest, and dropping it leaves Codex with a half install.
42	
43	**Trap: never put `rm -rf` in the install script.** The `dcg` PreToolUse guard
44	blocks the *entire* command on rule `core.filesystem:rm-rf-general`, even when the
45	target is a subfolder you just created yourself. Copy only what you want instead of
46	copy-then-delete. `dcg` also false-positives on a `>` inside a heredoc'd Python
47	script (rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`) — use the Edit tool for
48	that write rather than fighting the pattern.
49	
50	**Trap: a hand-install is invisible to the ledger.** It gets no entry in
51	`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`, so `skills update` will never touch it.
52	`skillFolderHash` is not a plain sha1 of the files and is not worth
53	reverse-engineering — have Eric run the official `add` command himself behind a `!`
54	prefix to register it.
55	
56	**Trap: `-a` will not take a comma-separated list.** `-a claude-code,codex`
57	fails with "Invalid agents: claude-code,codex" and then prints a valid-agent
58	list containing both names. Repeat the flag instead.
59	
60	**Trap: the installer does not always wire Codex.** It reports
61	`universal: Codex` and creates no symlink. Check
62	`ls -l ~/.codex/skills/<name>` after every install and make the symlink by hand
63	if it is missing.
64	
65	The CLI runs a security scan and may report alerts. Read
66	`https://skills.sh/<owner>/<repo>` before trusting a skill.
67	
68	**Cowork cannot take a locally-dropped skill.** Its store is
69	`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/skills-plugin/<a>/<b>/skills/`
70	with a sibling `manifest.json`, and every entry carries a **server-minted id**
71	(`skill_01…`). A folder placed there is not in the manifest and is wiped on the
72	next sync. The only route is a zip uploaded through claude.ai → Settings →
73	Capabilities → Skills, with the skill folder at the zip root. Expect Cowork's
74	sandbox to lack ffmpeg/Chrome, so any skill's verification or media step will
75	not run there even after a successful upload.
76	
77	Where a skill puts its *output* is separate: some resolve a workspace from the
78	nearest `.git` walking up, so run them from inside the target project or set
79	their env override, or builds land wherever cwd happened to be.
80	
81	See [[vendored-skill-repair]] for what to do when one of these is broken, and
82	[[path-shadowing-and-cleanup]] before deleting any copy.

2	name: ingest-review-gate
3	description: "Before any expensive, hard-to-inspect ingest (ingest-book atomization): a verification step plus an independent model review must pass first"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: feedback
7	  originSessionId: 4597514e-1de9-4f80-87b7-4c8742ddec83
8	  modified: 2026-09-05T14:57:33.666Z
9	---
10	
11	**Stated 2026-09-05**, finishing the Myszka book scan, when Eric was asked how much of the
12	pipeline could run on a cheaper model.
13	
14	**Do not run `/ingest-book` (or any comparable atomization) straight off a freshly built
15	artifact. Gate it on two things: an automated verification step, and a review by an
16	independent model — Codex, or a fresh adversarial agent if Codex is unavailable.**
17	
18	**Why:** the ingest is the expensive step *and* the one whose output is hardest to eyeball.
19	A page-order error costs almost nothing to make, is baked into the PDF, and is then
20	inherited silently by every note built from it. Eric's own framing: "cheap step, very
21	expensive mistake." He explicitly declined to cheapen the ingest itself, because that is
22	where judgement about what matters in the text happens.
23	
24	**How to apply:**
25	
26	- Build the artifact, then **verify by a route that shares no code path with how it was
27	  built.** For the book scan: the order was set by a *visual* read of cropped folio bands,
28	  so verification read the folio out of the *full-page OCR text* of the finished PDF, and a
29	  third pass rendered the PDF and read the folios off the rendered pages.
30	- **A cheap arithmetic identity is worth having, but do not oversell it.** `files −
31	  duplicates == last − first + 1` costs nothing; make it a hard gate that refuses to
32	  proceed, and test it with a deliberately corrupted input. **But it is a map-consistency
33	  check, not a proof of order.** On the default path — where folios are assigned as a
34	  running counter — the two sides of the identity are equal *by construction*, so the gate
35	  compares a number with itself. A transposition, a wrong start page, a missed duplicate,
36	  and two cancelling errors all pass it.
37	- **Audit the verification itself, not just the artifact.** The first version of
38	  `verify_pdf.py` "checked" that folios increase by appending the *expected* value and
39	  testing that those increased — true by construction, so it printed YES unconditionally.
40	  A check that cannot fail is worse than no check. **Prove a check can fail**: feed it a
41	  deliberately corrupted copy and confirm it says NO.
42	- **State coverage and blind spots in the output.** Six of 240 pages printed no folio and
43	  contributed no evidence; a uniform offset error is invisible to a folio check. Print
44	  that, do not imply 100%.
45	- Then hand it to the independent reviewer with an instruction to **falsify**, not confirm,
46	  and with the specific claims spelled out.
47	
48	**The related cheap-model decision (same conversation):** a small model may take the first
49	pass at reading page numbers off contact sheets, because the sheet prints the *expected*
50	number beside each crop — so the job is spotting disagreements, not reading every number.
51	Anything it flags, and anything ambiguous, gets a careful second look. Eric chose this
52	mainly for speed; he was explicit that the savings are small and **the gate is the part
53	worth keeping.**
54	
55	**What the gate actually caught, 2026-09-05.** The independent review returned **GO** on the
56	book PDF and **NO-GO** on the reference file shipped alongside it — which is the whole
57	argument for the gate in one result. It found: a verification check that was a tautology and
58	could never fail; an overstated claim about what the arithmetic gate proves; 7 chimeric
59	bibliography records welding one entry's authors to another's title; and 67 of 113 records
60	carrying a phantom author literally named "K". All were fixed before ingest. **The page order
61	was sound, and the thing shipped beside it was not** — so gate every deliverable, not just
62	the expensive one.
63	
64	Related: [[book-scan-page-ordering]] · [[keystoneos-verification-habits]]

3	description: "the SessionEnd memsearch hook read its path config from a Windows-era ~/Desktop/DEV path and silently fell back, indexing 4 of 10 memory paths for months after the Mac migration"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project

9	---
10	
11	`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` is the single source of truth for which directories memsearch indexes. Three writers read it: the SessionEnd hook `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (nightly; 09:00 since 2026-08-29), and the Codex hook `KeystoneOS/scripts/codex-hooks/memsearch-sync.ps1`.
12	
13	**Found 2026-08-14:** the JS hook pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` — the pre-migration Windows layout. DEV lives at `~/DEV` on this Mac, so the read threw, the `catch` returned a hardcoded fallback, and the hook indexed **4 paths instead of 10** for months. The fallback itself was also stale (`~/Desktop/SecondBrain/...`, which does not exist since the vault move). `daily-backup.ps1` used `$U/DEV` and was already correct; the Codex hook self-locates from its own script path and was fine. So only the JS hook drifted — and it is the one wired into `settings.json` (`SessionEnd`, 50s timeout).
14	
15	Unindexed as a result: `SecondBrain/Knowledge`, `SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings`, `SecondBrain/morning-briefings`, the Mac memory slug `-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory`, `KeystoneOS/decisions`, `.codex/memories`. Incremental recall for all of those depended entirely on that nightly.
16	
17	**Why:** the failure mode was invisible. A silent `catch → fallback` means a migration-broken config path degrades into a quieter, smaller, still-succeeding job — no error, no log line, no failed run. Nothing surfaces until someone asks "why didn't that turn up in search?" The bug was not the wrong path; it was that the wrong path cost nothing to have.
18	
19	**How to apply:**
20	- Any config-file fallback in this stack must log to `.errors.log` when it fires. The JS hook now does. A fallback that never announces itself is a silent outage with a long tail.
21	- When auditing post-migration breakage, grep for `Desktop/DEV` and `Desktop/SecondBrain` — those two strings mark Windows-era assumptions. Do not trust that a script "works" as evidence its paths resolved; check what it actually resolved to.
22	- Verify path config by resolving it in isolation (`node -e` reading the same JSON, printing EXISTS/MISSING per entry) rather than by running the indexer — that proves the fix without taking the Milvus Lite write lock.
23	- Paths in the JSON that do not exist yet are harmless; every writer filters through an existence check before passing them to memsearch.
24	
25	**There were TWO copies of this hook, and fixing one did not fix the other (2026-08-15).** A Codex review found `~/.codex/hooks.json` wires its *own* copy at `~/.codex/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, separate from the Claude copy at `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`. The Claude copy was repaired 2026-08-14; the Codex copy still pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/...`, so **every Codex session-end indexed a stale 5-path fallback** that also referenced the old `~/Desktop/SecondBrain` — missing SecondBrain/Knowledge, Inbox/meetings, morning-briefings, KeystoneOS decisions and the Mac memory slug. Now fixed and verified resolving all 11 configured paths.
26	
27	Ordering trap in that repair: `const ERR_LOG` was declared *after* `const PATHS = resolvePaths()`. Adding a `logErr()` call inside `resolvePaths` therefore hit the const temporal dead zone, and `logErr`'s own `try/catch` swallowed the ReferenceError — reproducing the silent fallback the fix was meant to remove. `ERR_LOG` must be declared before `PATHS`.
28	
29	**How to apply:** when fixing a hook, first ask *which copy the harness actually wires* — check `~/.codex/hooks.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json`, not just the file you happened to open. Grep the whole home tree for the hook's basename before assuming there is one.
30	
31	**A THIRD hook had the same stale path, found 2026-09-01 during `/doctor-plus`.** `~/.claude/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js` (SessionStart) read `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/unified-snapshot.md`, threw ENOENT, and its `catch (_) { emit(null) }` injected **nothing at all** — for every session since the migration. The snapshot file was being written correctly the whole time at `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/`; only the reader was wrong. Zero symptoms: no error, no log, valid JSON on stdout, session starts normally.
32	
33	The 2026-08-14/15 sweep fixed the two `memsearch-sync.js` copies but did not catch this one, so **"grep for `Desktop/DEV`" must cover every file in `~/.claude/hooks/` and `~/.codex/hooks/`, not only the hook currently being repaired.** Run it as a sweep across the whole hooks tree, not per-file.
34	
35	That sweep then found a **fourth** copy — `~/.codex/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js`, byte-identical and wired in `~/.codex/hooks.json`. Also fixed 2026-09-01.
36	
37	**A second signature the `Desktop/DEV` grep cannot catch:** `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (dated 2026-08-08) had been through a bad `claude` to `Codex` find-replace, so it told Codex to read `~/.Codex/global-memory/`, `~/.Codex/projects/<slug>/memory/` and `~/.Codex/Codex-memory-compiler/daily/` — none of which exist. Grep for `.Codex` (capital C) as well as `Desktop/DEV` when auditing migration damage. Also check which AGENTS.md the harness actually reads: `~/.claude/AGENTS.md` was correct but referenced by nothing.
38	
39	Resolved 2026-09-01: `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` is now a symlink to `~/.claude/AGENTS.md`, so the pair has one home and cannot drift again. `setup-agents-symlinks.sh` was also sourcing `CLAUDE.md` for that link — the one thing `CLAUDE.md` explicitly forbids — and now sources `AGENTS.md`. Running that script used to recreate the bug.
40	
41	Repaired 2026-09-01: path corrected to `~/DEV`, required sources now push a visible "SessionStart hook could not read a required memory file" block into `additionalContext` instead of failing silently, and the hook now also injects `global-memory/USER.md` + `MEMORY.md` (replacing a prose rule in `CLAUDE.md` that nothing enforced). The KeystoneOS snapshot is pointed at, not pasted.

11	Verified 2026-10-03 on the Baylor Windows laptop. Eric ran the tests himself; all passed.
12	
13	- **Microsoft Graph (delegated) works.** `Install-Module Microsoft.Graph.Authentication -Scope CurrentUser`, then `Connect-MgGraph -Scopes "User.Read","Mail.Read","Calendars.Read","Chat.Read"`. Baylor allowed the consent (unlike the Box connector, see [[box-access-via-box-drive]]). `/me`, `/me/messages` and `/me/chats` returned data via `Invoke-MgGraphRequest`. Teams write scopes (ChatMessage.Send, ChannelMessage.Send) are BLOCKED: sign-in asks for Baylor IT admin approval (tested 2026-10-03). Mail.Send and Calendars.ReadWrite are untested.
14	- **Office COM works from PowerShell** (FullLanguage mode, no admin): Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and classic Outlook (`Outlook.Application`, inbox read without a security prompt).
15	- New Outlook and new Teams are installed too. Neither has COM: Teams goes through Graph, and so would new Outlook mail.
16	- Teams posting workaround: a Teams Workflows webhook on a channel (posts as a bot). Eric created a private Team by hand 2026-10-03. NEXT: add the Workflows webhook to its channel, save the URL as the `TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL` user env var (never in chat or a repo), then write a posting script and send one test message.
17	- CLI-Anything (HKUDS) was reviewed and rejected for this: it targets open-source apps, and these are closed-source.
18	
19	**Why:** Saves re-testing access each session; Graph sign-in is interactive (browser), so the agent can't silently re-verify it.
20	**How to apply:** For file edits use the docx/pptx/xlsx skills; for app actions (recalc, PDF export, mail, calendar) use COM; for Teams use Graph. Graph needs Eric to sign in in the browser at the start of a session; ask before adding any send scope.

9	
10	CLI built and working at `~/printing-press/library/catapult` (binary: `catapult-pp-cli.exe`).
11	
12	**Why:** Sport scientist at Baylor Football needed programmatic access to GPS wearable data without R scripts or manual OpenField exports.
13	
14	## Critical API Discoveries (do not re-investigate)
15	
16	- **Correct base URL:** `https://connect-us.catapultsports.com/api/v6` (NOT v4 — v4 gives 404/405 on stats)
17	- **Stats endpoint:** `POST /stats` (NOT `/statistics` — that path doesn't work)
18	- **Auth:** Pre-generated JWT Bearer token from OpenField → Settings → API Tokens; set `CATAPULT_TOKEN` env var
19	- **Token scope matters:** Token with scopes `["connect"]` works. `["connect","catapultr","sensor-read-only"]` may not access stats.
20	- **Stats body:** `{"filters":[{"name":"activity_id","comparison":"=","values":["<uuid>"]}],"parameters":["average_player_load",...],"group_by":["athlete"]}`
21	- **Key slug:** `average_player_load` (NOT `total_player_load`) — v6 returns per-athlete session average
22	- **Date format from API:** `MM/DD/YYYY` — must normalize to `YYYY-MM-DD` before SQLite date comparisons
23	- **Statistics NOT bulk-syncable:** Must query per-activity; CLI uses Python bulk sync for historical data
24	
25	## What Works
26	
27	- `athletes`, `activities`, `parameters` — standard GET endpoints, work with any token
28	- `stats --activity <uuid> --metric <slugs> --group-by athlete` — live data, caches to local store
29	- `acwr --squad --metric average_player_load --date YYYY-MM-DD` — ACWR dashboard
30	- `pb --metric max_vel` — personal bests with trend
31	- `diff <activity1> <activity2> --metrics ...` — session comparison
32	- `report --from ... --to ... --squad` — weekly load summary
33	- `params search <keyword>` — FTS across 1,829 parameter slugs
34	
35	## Data Available (Baylor Football account)
36	
37	- 520 athletes, 2,522 activities, 1,829 parameters
38	- Last 30 days synced: 15 activities, 869 statistics rows (Spring 2026)
39	- Historical DB at `~/printing-press/.runstate/.../working/catapult-pp-cli/.env` (token file)
40	
41	## Known Nuances (from prior working system)
42	
43	- `max_vel` is in **mph** from API (multiply × 0.44704 to store as m/s)
44	- `velocity_band3_total_distance` = HSD (75–90% max vel), bands 5–8 return 0 for Baylor
45	- `average_player_load` slug = session average per athlete (misnamed; acts like total)
46	- Walk-throughs have near-zero velocity — filter by activity name when computing speed metrics
47	- ACWR values >3 at spring camp start are expected artifact (low chronic denominator)
48	
49	Superseded by the `pp-catapult-openfield-connect` skill for day-to-day use, but this file's API discoveries below remain the ground truth for the endpoints — don't re-investigate them.
50

11	**Standing permission, given 2026-09-26:** "I trust your judgement to remove things that are
12	safe to remove after merges." Once a PR is merged, clean up its worktree folders and its
13	local and remote branches without asking. Report what was removed in one line.
14	
15	**Why:** Leftover worktrees and merged branches had piled up in `RTP_Constraints_Course`:
16	three orphan worktree folders and seven merged branches from one day's PRs. Asking about
17	each one is friction he does not want.
18	
19	**How to apply:**
20	- "Safe" means verified, not assumed:
21	  - `git branch --merged origin/main` (and `-r`) lists a branch before it is deleted;
22	  - before deleting a worktree folder, every file in it is already in git history
23	    (`git hash-object --path=<rel> <file>`, looked up against `git rev-list --all --objects`);
24	  - there is no uncommitted work.
25	- **Anything unmerged, or holding content that is not in git, is out of scope. Ask.**
26	- The scope is post-merge git debris only. It does not cover deleting data, outputs, Drive
27	  files or anything else, and merging a PR still needs his ask.
28	- **Windows trap:** `git worktree remove`/`prune` fails with "Permission denied" because the
29	  folders carry a read-only attribute (probably from Drive sync), not a lock. Fix:
30	  `attrib -r /s /d` on both `.git\worktrees\<name>` and `.claude\worktrees\<name>`, then
31	  `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force` both folders, then `git worktree prune`. Written into
32	  `RTP_Constraints_Course/docs/STATUS.md` (PR #7).

2	name: third-party-skill-install
3	description: "How a vendored third-party skill installs across all five harnesses — clone into ~/.agents/skills, symlink out — plus the Windows ln -s copy trap and the pre-commit/daily-backup jam that sync-to-codex clears"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: 0804822d-4ddb-4933-801e-9a07f13445ae
8	  modified: 2026-09-18T18:12:58.161Z
9	---
10	
11	Installing a third-party (vendored, upstream-owned) skill on this setup: **clone the repo
12	into `~/.agents/skills/<name>` — the one real directory — then symlink it into the four
13	harness folders.** Established by the six that predate it (`humanizer`, `pp-espn`,
14	`articulation-skill`, `game-film-timestamps`, `pp-fireflies`, `session-handoff`).
15	
16	```
17	~/.agents/skills/<name>        ← the clone; Codex/Cursor/Copilot read here natively
18	~/.claude/skills/<name>   →    symlink    Claude Code
19	~/.gemini/skills/<name>   →    symlink    Gemini CLI
20	~/.codex/skills/<name>    →    symlink    Codex
21	~/.cursor/skills/<name>   →    symlink    Cursor
22	```
23	
24	One clone means one `git pull` updates every harness. Claude Code registers a new skill
25	**live, mid-session** — no restart needed.
26	
27	**Windows trap — `ln -s` silently copies.** Git Bash's default `ln -s` duplicates the
28	directory instead of linking. Claude Code still finds the skill, so it *looks* installed,
29	but the copy has no `.git` and `git pull` silently stops being the update path. Use
30	`MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict ln -s <target> <link>`, and verify from PowerShell —
31	`(Get-Item <path> -Force).LinkType` must print `SymbolicLink`. `ls -la` in Git Bash shows
32	`l... ->` for both cases, so it is **not** sufficient proof on its own. Same MSYS family as
33	[[git-bash-msys-ad-stall]], different mechanism.
34	
35	**The nightly-backup jam.** `~/.claude/skills` is its own repo with a `pre-commit` hook
36	that refuses any symlink (git mode 120000), while `daily-backup.ps1` runs `git add -A` on
37	it. So a freshly added third-party symlink sits as `?? <name>` and will **jam the nightly
38	backup commit** until the exclude block is regenerated.
39	
40	**The fix is `~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.ps1`, not a hand edit.** It classifies every
41	symlink in `~/.claude/skills` as THIRD_PARTY, drops it from the git index ("removed
42	third-party link '<name>' from the index (left on disk)"), and rewrites the generated block
43	in `.git/info/exclude` — which is marked *"Rewritten on every sync. Per-machine. Do not
44	edit by hand."* Supports `DRY_RUN=1`; dry-run first and confirm zero `retire`/`REFUSE`/
45	`FATAL` lines before applying.
46	
47	**Why the sync cannot clobber the clone:** its copy loop touches only `$MANAGED` entries
48	(real directories in canonical with a SKILL.md), and its retirement loop only removes names
49	present in the *previous* manifest. A third-party name enters neither list, so
50	`~/.agents/skills/<name>` and its `.git` survive every sync. Verified — sync ran clean over
51	41 managed + 7 third-party with the clone intact on `main`.
52	
53	**Do not route these through `CreateSkill`.** Canonicalizing an upstream repo (TitleCase,
54	`Workflows/`) rewrites files git tracks and breaks `git pull`. The `skills/CLAUDE.md`
55	mandate governs skills Eric *owns*, not vendored ones.
56	
57	**Nothing propagates to the Mac.** `skills/` is gitignored out of the dotclaude repo and
58	`~/.agents` is not a repo at all, so each machine needs its own clone + symlinks.
59	
60	Established 2026-09-18 installing `grill-with-ui`. Related:
61	[[dev-layout-and-discovery]], [[keystoneos-verification-habits]]
62

2	name: vendored-skill-install
3	description: "Installing a third-party skill so Claude Code, Codex and Cowork can all use it — the canonical store, the two symlinks, the CLI flag trap, and why Cowork is different"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: a6dfb3da-c339-44b1-a836-2a6884e07ea6
8	  modified: 2026-09-04T13:43:21.110Z
9	---
10	
11	Third-party skills live in **`~/.agents/skills/<name>/`** (the real files, ~360 of
12	them) with `~/.agents/.skill-lock.json` as the install ledger. Both harness
13	directories are symlinks into it:
14	
15	- `~/.claude/skills/<name>` → `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (relative)
16	- `~/.codex/skills/<name>` → `~/.claude/skills/<name>` (absolute, hopping through
17	  the Claude symlink — verified on disk 2026-09-04. It does **not** point straight
18	  at `~/.agents/skills/`.)
19	
20	Install with the CLI that owns that store when you can:
21	
22	```bash
23	npx -y skills@latest add <owner>/<repo> -g -a claude-code -a codex -s <skill> -y
24	```
25	
26	**Trap: in Claude Code auto mode the CLI itself is blocked.** The permission
27	classifier denies `npx -y skills@latest add …` outright (hit 2026-09-04).
28	Hand-install is then the working route, and it is enough — the files plus the two
29	symlinks are all a harness needs:
30	
31	```bash
32	mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills/NAME
33	cp REPO/CAT/NAME/SKILL.md ~/.agents/skills/NAME/
34	cp -R REPO/CAT/NAME/scripts REPO/CAT/NAME/agents ~/.agents/skills/NAME/   # when present
35	chmod +x ~/.agents/skills/NAME/scripts/*.sh
36	ln -s ../../.agents/skills/NAME ~/.claude/skills/NAME
37	ln -s ~/.claude/skills/NAME ~/.codex/skills/NAME
38	```
39	
40	Copy `agents/openai.yaml` too whenever the skill ships one — it is the
41	Codex-facing manifest, and dropping it leaves Codex with a half install.
42	
43	**Trap: never put `rm -rf` in the install script.** The `dcg` PreToolUse guard
44	blocks the *entire* command on rule `core.filesystem:rm-rf-general`, even when the
45	target is a subfolder you just created yourself. Copy only what you want instead of
46	copy-then-delete. `dcg` also false-positives on a `>` inside a heredoc'd Python
47	script (rule `core.filesystem:redirect-truncate-root-home`) — use the Edit tool for
48	that write rather than fighting the pattern.
49	
50	**Trap: a hand-install is invisible to the ledger.** It gets no entry in
51	`~/.agents/.skill-lock.json`, so `skills update` will never touch it.
52	`skillFolderHash` is not a plain sha1 of the files and is not worth
53	reverse-engineering — have Eric run the official `add` command himself behind a `!`
54	prefix to register it.
55	
56	**Trap: `-a` will not take a comma-separated list.** `-a claude-code,codex`
57	fails with "Invalid agents: claude-code,codex" and then prints a valid-agent
58	list containing both names. Repeat the flag instead.
59	
60	**Trap: the installer does not always wire Codex.** It reports
61	`universal: Codex` and creates no symlink. Check
62	`ls -l ~/.codex/skills/<name>` after every install and make the symlink by hand
63	if it is missing.
64	
65	The CLI runs a security scan and may report alerts. Read
66	`https://skills.sh/<owner>/<repo>` before trusting a skill.
67	
68	**Cowork cannot take a locally-dropped skill.** Its store is
69	`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/local-agent-mode-sessions/skills-plugin/<a>/<b>/skills/`
70	with a sibling `manifest.json`, and every entry carries a **server-minted id**
71	(`skill_01…`). A folder placed there is not in the manifest and is wiped on the
72	next sync. The only route is a zip uploaded through claude.ai → Settings →
73	Capabilities → Skills, with the skill folder at the zip root. Expect Cowork's
74	sandbox to lack ffmpeg/Chrome, so any skill's verification or media step will
75	not run there even after a successful upload.
76	
77	Where a skill puts its *output* is separate: some resolve a workspace from the
78	nearest `.git` walking up, so run them from inside the target project or set
79	their env override, or builds land wherever cwd happened to be.
80	
81	See [[vendored-skill-repair]] for what to do when one of these is broken, and
82	[[path-shadowing-and-cleanup]] before deleting any copy.
83

2	name: ingest-review-gate
3	description: "Before any expensive, hard-to-inspect ingest (ingest-book atomization): a verification step plus an independent model review must pass first"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: feedback
7	  originSessionId: 4597514e-1de9-4f80-87b7-4c8742ddec83
8	  modified: 2026-09-05T14:57:33.666Z
9	---
10	
11	**Stated 2026-09-05**, finishing the Myszka book scan, when Eric was asked how much of the
12	pipeline could run on a cheaper model.
13	
14	**Do not run `/ingest-book` (or any comparable atomization) straight off a freshly built
15	artifact. Gate it on two things: an automated verification step, and a review by an
16	independent model — Codex, or a fresh adversarial agent if Codex is unavailable.**
17	
18	**Why:** the ingest is the expensive step *and* the one whose output is hardest to eyeball.
19	A page-order error costs almost nothing to make, is baked into the PDF, and is then
20	inherited silently by every note built from it. Eric's own framing: "cheap step, very
21	expensive mistake." He explicitly declined to cheapen the ingest itself, because that is
22	where judgement about what matters in the text happens.
23	
24	**How to apply:**
25	
26	- Build the artifact, then **verify by a route that shares no code path with how it was
27	  built.** For the book scan: the order was set by a *visual* read of cropped folio bands,
28	  so verification read the folio out of the *full-page OCR text* of the finished PDF, and a
29	  third pass rendered the PDF and read the folios off the rendered pages.
30	- **A cheap arithmetic identity is worth having, but do not oversell it.** `files −
31	  duplicates == last − first + 1` costs nothing; make it a hard gate that refuses to
32	  proceed, and test it with a deliberately corrupted input. **But it is a map-consistency
33	  check, not a proof of order.** On the default path — where folios are assigned as a
34	  running counter — the two sides of the identity are equal *by construction*, so the gate
35	  compares a number with itself. A transposition, a wrong start page, a missed duplicate,
36	  and two cancelling errors all pass it.
37	- **Audit the verification itself, not just the artifact.** The first version of
38	  `verify_pdf.py` "checked" that folios increase by appending the *expected* value and
39	  testing that those increased — true by construction, so it printed YES unconditionally.
40	  A check that cannot fail is worse than no check. **Prove a check can fail**: feed it a
41	  deliberately corrupted copy and confirm it says NO.
42	- **State coverage and blind spots in the output.** Six of 240 pages printed no folio and
43	  contributed no evidence; a uniform offset error is invisible to a folio check. Print
44	  that, do not imply 100%.
45	- Then hand it to the independent reviewer with an instruction to **falsify**, not confirm,
46	  and with the specific claims spelled out.
47	
48	**The related cheap-model decision (same conversation):** a small model may take the first
49	pass at reading page numbers off contact sheets, because the sheet prints the *expected*
50	number beside each crop — so the job is spotting disagreements, not reading every number.
51	Anything it flags, and anything ambiguous, gets a careful second look. Eric chose this
52	mainly for speed; he was explicit that the savings are small and **the gate is the part
53	worth keeping.**
54	
55	**What the gate actually caught, 2026-09-05.** The independent review returned **GO** on the
56	book PDF and **NO-GO** on the reference file shipped alongside it — which is the whole
57	argument for the gate in one result. It found: a verification check that was a tautology and
58	could never fail; an overstated claim about what the arithmetic gate proves; 7 chimeric
59	bibliography records welding one entry's authors to another's title; and 67 of 113 records
60	carrying a phantom author literally named "K". All were fixed before ingest. **The page order
61	was sound, and the thing shipped beside it was not** — so gate every deliverable, not just
62	the expensive one.
63	
64	Related: [[book-scan-page-ordering]] · [[keystoneos-verification-habits]]
65

2	name: memsearch-index-path-drift
3	description: "the SessionEnd memsearch hook read its path config from a Windows-era ~/Desktop/DEV path and silently fell back, indexing 4 of 10 memory paths for months after the Mac migration"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  modified: 2026-08-15T04:07:30.329Z
8	  originSessionId: 75381393-88b6-4b65-960d-6613e08f7060
9	---
10	
11	`~/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` is the single source of truth for which directories memsearch indexes. Three writers read it: the SessionEnd hook `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1` (nightly; 09:00 since 2026-08-29), and the Codex hook `KeystoneOS/scripts/codex-hooks/memsearch-sync.ps1`.
12	
13	**Found 2026-08-14:** the JS hook pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` — the pre-migration Windows layout. DEV lives at `~/DEV` on this Mac, so the read threw, the `catch` returned a hardcoded fallback, and the hook indexed **4 paths instead of 10** for months. The fallback itself was also stale (`~/Desktop/SecondBrain/...`, which does not exist since the vault move). `daily-backup.ps1` used `$U/DEV` and was already correct; the Codex hook self-locates from its own script path and was fine. So only the JS hook drifted — and it is the one wired into `settings.json` (`SessionEnd`, 50s timeout).
14	
15	Unindexed as a result: `SecondBrain/Knowledge`, `SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings`, `SecondBrain/morning-briefings`, the Mac memory slug `-Users-kristinarash-DEV/memory`, `KeystoneOS/decisions`, `.codex/memories`. Incremental recall for all of those depended entirely on that nightly.
16	
17	**Why:** the failure mode was invisible. A silent `catch → fallback` means a migration-broken config path degrades into a quieter, smaller, still-succeeding job — no error, no log line, no failed run. Nothing surfaces until someone asks "why didn't that turn up in search?" The bug was not the wrong path; it was that the wrong path cost nothing to have.
18	
19	**How to apply:**
20	- Any config-file fallback in this stack must log to `.errors.log` when it fires. The JS hook now does. A fallback that never announces itself is a silent outage with a long tail.
21	- When auditing post-migration breakage, grep for `Desktop/DEV` and `Desktop/SecondBrain` — those two strings mark Windows-era assumptions. Do not trust that a script "works" as evidence its paths resolved; check what it actually resolved to.
22	- Verify path config by resolving it in isolation (`node -e` reading the same JSON, printing EXISTS/MISSING per entry) rather than by running the indexer — that proves the fix without taking the Milvus Lite write lock.
23	- Paths in the JSON that do not exist yet are harmless; every writer filters through an existence check before passing them to memsearch.
24	
25	**There were TWO copies of this hook, and fixing one did not fix the other (2026-08-15).** A Codex review found `~/.codex/hooks.json` wires its *own* copy at `~/.codex/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`, separate from the Claude copy at `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`. The Claude copy was repaired 2026-08-14; the Codex copy still pointed at `~/Desktop/DEV/...`, so **every Codex session-end indexed a stale 5-path fallback** that also referenced the old `~/Desktop/SecondBrain` — missing SecondBrain/Knowledge, Inbox/meetings, morning-briefings, KeystoneOS decisions and the Mac memory slug. Now fixed and verified resolving all 11 configured paths.
26	
27	Ordering trap in that repair: `const ERR_LOG` was declared *after* `const PATHS = resolvePaths()`. Adding a `logErr()` call inside `resolvePaths` therefore hit the const temporal dead zone, and `logErr`'s own `try/catch` swallowed the ReferenceError — reproducing the silent fallback the fix was meant to remove. `ERR_LOG` must be declared before `PATHS`.
28	
29	**How to apply:** when fixing a hook, first ask *which copy the harness actually wires* — check `~/.codex/hooks.json` and `~/.claude/settings.json`, not just the file you happened to open. Grep the whole home tree for the hook's basename before assuming there is one.
30	
31	**A THIRD hook had the same stale path, found 2026-09-01 during `/doctor-plus`.** `~/.claude/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js` (SessionStart) read `~/Desktop/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/unified-snapshot.md`, threw ENOENT, and its `catch (_) { emit(null) }` injected **nothing at all** — for every session since the migration. The snapshot file was being written correctly the whole time at `~/DEV/KeystoneOS/outputs/dashboard/`; only the reader was wrong. Zero symptoms: no error, no log, valid JSON on stdout, session starts normally.
32	
33	The 2026-08-14/15 sweep fixed the two `memsearch-sync.js` copies but did not catch this one, so **"grep for `Desktop/DEV`" must cover every file in `~/.claude/hooks/` and `~/.codex/hooks/`, not only the hook currently being repaired.** Run it as a sweep across the whole hooks tree, not per-file.
34	
35	That sweep then found a **fourth** copy — `~/.codex/hooks/keystone-unified-snapshot.js`, byte-identical and wired in `~/.codex/hooks.json`. Also fixed 2026-09-01.
36

2	name: catapult-cli
3	description: "Catapult Connect CLI built with Printing Press — key API discoveries, CLI location, and what works"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project

8	---
9	
10	CLI built and working at `~/printing-press/library/catapult` (binary: `catapult-pp-cli.exe`).
11	
12	**Why:** Sport scientist at Baylor Football needed programmatic access to GPS wearable data without R scripts or manual OpenField exports.
13	
14	## Critical API Discoveries (do not re-investigate)
15	
16	- **Correct base URL:** `https://connect-us.catapultsports.com/api/v6` (NOT v4 — v4 gives 404/405 on stats)
17	- **Stats endpoint:** `POST /stats` (NOT `/statistics` — that path doesn't work)
18	- **Auth:** Pre-generated JWT Bearer token from OpenField → Settings → API Tokens; set `CATAPULT_TOKEN` env var
19	- **Token scope matters:** Token with scopes `["connect"]` works. `["connect","catapultr","sensor-read-only"]` may not access stats.
20	- **Stats body:** `{"filters":[{"name":"activity_id","comparison":"=","values":["<uuid>"]}],"parameters":["average_player_load",...],"group_by":["athlete"]}`
21	- **Key slug:** `average_player_load` (NOT `total_player_load`) — v6 returns per-athlete session average
22	- **Date format from API:** `MM/DD/YYYY` — must normalize to `YYYY-MM-DD` before SQLite date comparisons
23	- **Statistics NOT bulk-syncable:** Must query per-activity; CLI uses Python bulk sync for historical data
24	
25	## What Works
26	
27	- `athletes`, `activities`, `parameters` — standard GET endpoints, work with any token
28	- `stats --activity <uuid> --metric <slugs> --group-by athlete` — live data, caches to local store
29	- `acwr --squad --metric average_player_load --date YYYY-MM-DD` — ACWR dashboard
30	- `pb --metric max_vel` — personal bests with trend
31	- `diff <activity1> <activity2> --metrics ...` — session comparison
32	- `report --from ... --to ... --squad` — weekly load summary
33	- `params search <keyword>` — FTS across 1,829 parameter slugs
34	
35	## Data Available (Baylor Football account)
36	
37	- 520 athletes, 2,522 activities, 1,829 parameters
38	- Last 30 days synced: 15 activities, 869 statistics rows (Spring 2026)
39	- Historical DB at `~/printing-press/.runstate/.../working/catapult-pp-cli/.env` (token file)
40	
41	## Known Nuances (from prior working system)
42	
43	- `max_vel` is in **mph** from API (multiply × 0.44704 to store as m/s)
44	- `velocity_band3_total_distance` = HSD (75–90% max vel), bands 5–8 return 0 for Baylor
45	- `average_player_load` slug = session average per athlete (misnamed; acts like total)
46	- Walk-throughs have near-zero velocity — filter by activity name when computing speed metrics
47	- ACWR values >3 at spring camp start are expected artifact (low chronic denominator)
48	
49	Superseded by the `pp-catapult-openfield-connect` skill for day-to-day use, but this file's API discoveries below remain the ground truth for the endpoints — don't re-investigate them.

  prefix. Never bundle it with a push: dcg rejects the whole line and the push is lost.

Installing a third-party (vendored, upstream-owned) skill on this setup: **clone the repo
into `~/.agents/skills/<name>` — the one real directory — then symlink it into the four
harness folders.** Established by the six that predate it (`humanizer`, `pp-espn`,
`articulation-skill`, `game-film-timestamps`, `pp-fireflies`, `session-handoff`).

```
~/.agents/skills/<name>        ← the clone; Codex/Cursor/Copilot read here natively
~/.claude/skills/<name>   →    symlink    Claude Code
~/.gemini/skills/<name>   →    symlink    Gemini CLI
~/.codex/skills/<name>    →    symlink    Codex
~/.cursor/skills/<name>   →    symlink    Cursor
```

One clone means one `git pull` updates every harness.

input.old_string:
- **A cheap arithmetic identity is worth having, but do not oversell it.** `files −
  duplicates == last − first + 1` costs nothing; make it a hard gate that refuses to
  proceed, and test it with a deliberately corrupted input. **But it is a map-consistency
  check, not a proof of order.** On the default path — where folios are assigned as a
  running counter — the two sides of the identity are equal *by construction*, so the gate
  compares a number with itself. A transposition, a wrong start page, a missed duplicate,
  and two cancelling errors all pass it.
input.new_string:

  order.** Why, with the Myszka evidence: [[book-scan-page-ordering]].

content.content:
Layout and install steps (real files in `~/.agents/skills/<name>`, symlinked out; checked
on the Mac): see [[vendored-skill-install]]. This file covers what happens after.

One clone means one `git pull` updates every harness. Claude Code registers a new skill
**live, mid-session** — no restart needed.

**Windows trap — `ln -s` silently copies** (historical: the laptop has had no terminal work
since 2026-10-14, see [[work-laptop-hands-off]]). Git Bash's default `ln -s` duplicates the
directory instead of linking. Claude Code still finds the skill, so it *looks* installed,
but the copy has no `.git` and `git pull` silently stops being the update path. Use
`MSYS=winsymlinks:nativestrict ln -s <target> <link>`, and verify from PowerShell —
`(Get-Item <path> -Force).LinkType` must print `SymbolicLink`. `ls -la` in Git Bash shows
`l... ->` for both cases, so it is **not** sufficient proof on its own. Same MSYS family as
[[git-bash-msys-ad-stall]], different mechanism.

**The daily-backup jam.** `~/.claude/skills` is its own repo with a `pre-commit` hook
that refuses any symlink (git mode 120000), while `daily-backup.ps1` runs `git add -A` on
it. So a freshly added third-party symlink sits as `?? <name>` and will **jam the daily
backup commit** until the exclude block is regenerated.

**The fix is `bash ~/.claude/skills/sync-to-codex.sh` on the Mac, not a hand edit**
(`sync-to-codex.ps1` is the Windows twin). It classifies every
symlink in `~/.claude/skills` as THIRD_PARTY, drops it from the git index ("removed
third-party link '<name>' from the index (left on disk)"), and rewrites the generated block
in `.git/info/exclude` — which is marked *"Rewritten on every sync. Per-machine. Do not
edit by hand."* Supports `DRY_RUN=1`; dry-run first and confirm zero `retire`/`REFUSE`/
`FATAL` lines before applying.

**Why the sync cannot clobber the clone:** its copy loop touches only `$MANAGED` entries
(real directories in canonical with a SKILL.md), and its retirement loop only removes names
present in the *previous* manifest. A third-party name enters neither list, so
`~/.agents/skills/<name>` and its `.git` survive every sync. Verified — sync ran clean over
41 managed + 7 third-party with the clone intact on `main`.

**Do not route these through `CreateSkill`.** Canonicalizing an upstream repo (TitleCase,
`Workflows/`) rewrites files git tracks and breaks `git pull`. The `skills/CLAUDE.md`
mandate governs skills Eric *owns*, not vendored ones.

**A third-party install never reaches the other machine.** Corrected 2026-10-24: the
reason is not the dotclaude gitignore. `~/.claude/skills/` is its own git repo
(`erash11/claude-skills`), and owned skills do travel through it
([[skill-bloat-and-promotion]]). But the sync above keeps third-party links out of that
repo on purpose, and `~/.agents` is not a repo at all. So each machine needs its own install.

Established 2026-09-18 installing `grill-with-ui`. Related:
[[dev-layout-and-discovery]], [[keystoneos-verification-habits]]


**Standing permission, given 2026-09-26:** "I trust your judgement to remove things that are
safe to remove after merges." Once a PR is merged, clean up its worktree folders and its
local and remote branches without asking. Report what was removed in one line.

**Corrected 2026-10-24: local branch deletes are Eric's to run.** The dcg guard keeps
`core.git:branch-force-delete` as a hard stop (Eric's choice, 2026-10-11). It blocks plain
`git branch -d` too (`dcg explain`, 2026-10-24). See [[dcg-guard-blocks]]. So:
- Do unasked: `git worktree remove` / `prune` and `git push origin --delete <branch>`.
  Both pass dcg.
- For local branches, give Eric the exact `git branch -d <names>` line to run with a `!`
  prefix. Never bundle it with a push: dcg rejects the whole line and the push is lost.

**Why:** Leftover worktrees and merged branches had piled up in `RTP_Constraints_Course`:
three orphan worktree folders and seven merged branches from one day's PRs. Asking about
each one is friction he does not want.
